A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KVTP and SparseKV-QA study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaVA-Video-7B/72B evaluations, component comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, ablations, and qualitative results, including Tables 2–4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same SigLIP relevance predictor, local/global context fusion, training objective, and conversion of relevance scores into frame-specific token-pruning rates.

E1.justification: Both versions construct SparseKV-QA from the same seven source datasets and evaluate on the same VideoMME, EgoSchema, and NeXT-QA subsets. The qualitative scenarios also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the original-model, Random Sampling, ToMe, PruMerge, KeyVideoLLM, and FastV comparisons and the same KVTP combinations. Table 4 retains GPT Assigned, KeyVideoLLM, and KVTP.

E3.justification: The training/evaluation split, 7B/72B backbones, accuracy and relative-FLOPs metrics, and 128-frame profiling remain unchanged. Baseline settings and the sparsity and temperature sweeps are also identical.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 retains the same keyframe-sparsity, selection-temperature, and relevance-predictor comparisons. Figure 3 and Appendix B retain identical qualitative cases; Figure 3 is only relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting changes appear in the appendices.

E6.justification: All table values, plotted results, and qualitative answers remain unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains PruMerge+Ours accuracies of 63.29, 54.71, and 76.76 on VideoMME, EgoSchema, and NextQA at 36% of baseline FLOPs.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), including relevance normalization, contextual attention, weighted logits, and the loss, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and method contributions, including the claims of pruning 80% of video tokens and reducing FLOPs by 64% while preserving performance.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations concerning temporal/contextual continuity, hard-selection failures, spatial redundancy, and domain shift. The emphasis on videos with sparse key information is unchanged.

D1.justification: Sampling, model, and profiling details remain identical. Appendix A retains the same constructed example and captioning/scoring prompts, and the code hyperlink has the same target.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chai et al.'s AuroraCap paper as reference [2] in Section 2.1's overview of video-language research. This is a limited citation addition; the surrounding discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The author block adds Guangzhi Su and Duke Kunshan University. Citation numbering and text flow change, while the substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 2's right column to page 3's left column with the same image and caption. The opening pages and references reflow; table structures and the remaining visual content are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds an author affiliation and one background citation and makes limited layout adjustments. The method, experimental evidence, mathematical content, reproducibility information, and appendices remain unchanged. These attribution and presentation updates leave the paper's overall scientific support and explanatory substance equivalent.
